summary.intent: Add a `delegate` role so an account owner can grant and revoke another user's read-only statement access, per issue #5.
summary.issue_fit: Met — all five acceptance criteria in issue #5 hold: owner-only grant/revoke that leaves state unchanged on refusal, delegate view scoped to only the granting account, delegates never post, and owner/auditor/teller access is untouched.
summary.coverage: Complete merge-base diff reviewed (ledger/accounts.py, ledger/auth.py, tests/test_delegates.py); no file ignored or unreviewed. Focused test tests/test_delegates.py run once at head a13922e: 3/3 pass. Full suite (`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`) also run once at head: 17/17 pass, no regression.

findings.title: Move the owner check for grant/revoke into ledger/auth.py
findings.trigger: Any call to Ledger.grant or Ledger.revoke.
findings.impact: Authorization decisions end up split across two modules: a future change to who may administer delegate access (e.g. letting a co-owner grant) requires editing accounts.py in two places instead of the single ledger/auth.py surface every other permission check uses, and the ownership comparison is duplicated verbatim in both methods.
findings.change: Add an ledger/auth.py function (for example can_manage_delegates(user, account)) that encapsulates the ownership check, and have Ledger.grant/Ledger.revoke call it instead of comparing account.owner to user themselves.

findings.title: Document the unknown-account error in grant/revoke docstrings
findings.trigger: Calling Ledger.grant or Ledger.revoke with a number that is not in self.accounts.
findings.impact: A reader relying on the docstring, per AGENTS.md's convention that every public function's docstring names the errors it raises, cannot tell from grant/revoke's docstring that an unknown account also raises LedgerError, unlike post's and transfer's docstrings, which enumerate that cause explicitly.
findings.change: Reword each docstring to name both causes, e.g. "Raises LedgerError for an unknown account or when user does not own it."

observations.fact: ledger/cli.py has no notion of a caller's identity or role, so the new delegate role and Ledger.grant/revoke are reachable only through the library API, not through the shipped `statement` command.
observations.evidence: ledger/cli.py:35-44 (main() calls render_statement(ledger.get(args.account)) unconditionally, with no user/role argument).
